source.description:

sentences.text: But You know, I'm aware that they're trying to hand down wealth taxes and they're kind of ruining the budget.

before.text: How likely do you think it is that something like that could happen in the United States?
And what should savers be watching for?

So what we've seen time and time again is we think that there's this line in the sand where a Western nation would not do something retroactive, where they will give you notice in advance and you can take some kind of action before.
But the truth is, whenever any economy, any government that overspends and gets out over their skis gets stressed, they do cross that line over and over and over again.
So the reason that I wrote about Italy, which is just not... classics like Lebanon or Argentina or Cyprus or any of these others from kind of Bitcoin lore.
What was interesting about that one is they did it retroactively.
So they did it based on balances from a few days before and didn't give you a chance to do anything about it.
And I do think that I'm obviously a proud resident of the California Socialist Republic.

after.text: And I could see them like why there's no rule that they can't do something.
It would be super unpopular, but there isn't a rule hard and fast that says they couldn't legislate something that was retroactive.
And I just wanted to wake people up to the fact that retroactive taxes and retroactive confiscation actually is a common pattern, even though we haven't seen it very recently in the West.
And, Corey, on that topic, you know, midterms are today, obviously, the nature of what we were just discussing is innately political, right?
This idea that governments are going to regulate.
They are going to exert their authority.
What's your outlook for the midterms?
And what do you make of sort of the politicalization around our industry over recent years?
Boy, that is a, that's a meaty topic that I've written about and talked about at length.
I'll try to do a very short version of it.
So I think there was a bit of a devil's bargain made by some in the Bitcoin industry, some of whom had large megaphones, basically to get in bed with one party.
